entities.summary:
Bernardino Ochino (1487–1564) emerged as one of the most intellectually restless and peripatetic figures of the Italian Reformation, a period marked by profound theological upheaval across Europe. Born in Siena, he rose to prominence as a highly respected Capuchin vicar-general, renowned for his eloquent preaching and spiritual fervor. His dramatic conversion from Roman Catholicism to Protestantism in the 1540s, driven by a deep engagement with Reformed theology, transformed him into a leading voice for evangelical reform, forcing him into a decades-long exile that spanned Switzerland, England, Germany, and Poland. His life exemplifies the profound personal and intellectual struggles faced by many during the 16th-century religious schism, challenging established doctrines and risking everything for theological conviction.

Ochino's journey began within the Observant Franciscans, then the Capuchins, where he became a celebrated preacher, serving as vicar-general in 1538 and 1541. His embrace of justification by faith alone, influenced by figures like Juan de Valdés and Pietro Martire Vermigli, led to his flight from Italy in 1542 to avoid the Roman Inquisition. He found refuge in Geneva under John Calvin, then moved to Augsburg, Strassburg, and eventually England in 1547, where he received a prebend at Canterbury and published several influential works under Edward VI. Following Mary I's Catholic restoration in 1553, Ochino fled again, settling in Zürich, where he served an Italian congregation and engaged in further theological writing, including dialogues on predestination and polygamy that sparked significant controversy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bernardino Ochino's journey from revered Catholic preacher to radical Protestant exile profoundly influenced the Italian Reformation and contributed significantly to the intellectual ferment of early Protestantism. His controversial writings and challenging theological positions, particularly on the Trinity, prefigured later heterodox movements and showcased the intense intellectual struggles of the era.
